lines.text: Why does my phone ignore me in gloves?
Because it can't feel you. At all.
Rude. I'm right here!
Under the glass is a grid of tiny invisible wires.
They hold a little electric charge, all the time.
Your skin conducts. So when you touch, some charge flows into your finger.
The grid feels that dip, right there. That's your tap.
So my finger steals electricity?
A tiny bit. Yes. Every tap.
Wool and leather don't conduct. The charge has nowhere to go.
So to the screen, you're just not there.
I'm a ghost!
A ghost with very warm hands.
Wait. Would a sausage work?
Yep. It's salty and wet, so it conducts. People really tried it.
I'm bringing a hot dog to the bus stop.
Please don't.
Get touchscreen gloves. The fingertips have conductive thread sewn in.
The charge runs through the thread into you, and the tap lands.
Or I just use my nose.
Sure. And now you know.
Ugh. It's so cold out, and...
